name: Metoprolol
summary: A cardioselective beta blocker used for rate control, angina, hypertension, and selected heart-failure regimens.
good: Patients who need rate control or a beta blocker with beta-1 selectivity.
bad: Marked bradycardia, conduction disease, or severe bronchospasm risk.
clinicalPearls: Tartrate and succinate are not interchangeable in every clinical context — the formulation matters.
mechanism: Blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors, lowering heart rate, contractility, and renin release.
indications: Rate control, angina, post-MI therapy, hypertension, and heart failure depending on formulation.
interactionNotes: Verapamil, diltiazem, and other rate-slowing drugs can stack bradycardia or conduction delay.

warnings: Bradycardia, fatigue, AV block, and caution in asthma/COPD or brittle diabetes.
